g.text: The dawn city bus / runs with its windows decked in some dazzling finery. / The harsher the dead of winter, / the more vividly the frost
flowers bloom. / Those who rode this bus yesterday / maidens and bachelors, children and grown-ups, / hairdressers, salesmen, housemaids,
the jobless / their breath and their sighs / met in secret overnight and brought forth / this flashing, breathtaking beauty. / As if I had
wandered into some exhibition, / I move
from seat to seat to look, / and once
again I am drunk on a single petal, / on
its delicate and cold beauty. / Whose
desolate sigh was this? / What warm
heart breathed out this breath of
passion? / For no reason, carefully, with
my breath and my finger, / I wipe away
a single frost petal / and press my
forehead to the glass. / A haggard face
friend, you walked the road beside me
for so long, / and now I am not even
